item.title: Do you really need an AI wearable to remember every moment?
item.dc:creator: Lucia
item.description: Editor’s Note: Human memory is selective, while digital devices can capture far more than we can remember. Wearable AI cameras take this a step further, recording everyday moments and using AI to organize them into personal recaps and insights. Looki is among the startups exploring this idea with its wearable camera, the L1. Early reviews […]
item.content:encoded:
Editor’s Note: Human memory is selective, while digital devices can capture far more than we can remember. Wearable AI cameras take this a step further, recording everyday moments and using AI to organize them into personal recaps and insights. Looki is among the startups exploring this idea with its wearable camera, the L1. Early reviews point to both the appeal of revisiting forgotten moments and the challenges of making sense of them, from missed context to privacy concerns. Can AI make our memories more useful, and what trade-offs come with letting it document our lives?

Human memory is sometimes a poor recording device. A commute blurs, a conversation loses its edges, and small moments vanish before we know they mattered. What remains is selective, shaped by emotion as much as fact. The latest attempt to capture these fleeting moments comes in the form of wearable AI cameras. Looki’s L1 is one of a growing number of devices in this emerging category. It records snippets of daily life, which its app can later assemble into summaries, visual stories, and daily recaps.

A Day Recut—and Reassessed

In a review for GameRevolution, Mack Ashworth found that the L1 could turn daily footage into recap videos, though the results were not always consistent. Some compilations offered a good overview of his day, while others were so short that they contained little to revisit.

Tom’s Guide’s Elton Jones had a more entertaining experience during his two-week trial. The device captured scenes from his commute, workday and journey home, which the app turned into a daily vlog and a comic strip. Jones particularly enjoyed seeing ordinary moments, such as grabbing lunch, reimagined as comic-book panels.

Jones also tested the L1’s food-tracking feature. After observing his lunch habits, the device generated nutritional breakdowns, compared meals across several days and suggested dietary adjustments.

While Jones found the feedback useful, his experience also raises questions about how accurately a wearable camera can assess someone’s eating habits from visual information alone.

The Cost of Being Remembered

Automatic capture also creates social friction. Stein described feeling awkward in public and worrying that people nearby did not know they might be recorded. Bystanders have little control over whether their image or conversations enter someone else’s private archive.

Looki says the L1 is not continuous by default and that its Trust Light blinks while recording. Its support FAQ says footage stays on the device until users choose to sync. The company’s privacy policy says personal content is not used to train general AI models and can be deleted on request. Looki also says it completed a SOC 2 Type I audit in 2026 and is working toward Type II.

But these measures do not settle consent in shared spaces. Looki’s policy puts responsibility for obtaining permissions on users.

Different Ways to Remember

Looki is exploring one way to build a personal AI memory, using visual recordings to capture everyday scenes, from places and activities to objects and interactions. Its L1 turns these clips into searchable records, daily vlogs and comic-style recaps.

Other companies are approaching the idea through sound. Amazon’s Bee Frontier uses recorded conversations to generate summaries and reminders. Plaud’s NotePin S organizes meetings and conversations into transcripts and notes, while Omi makes recorded conversations searchable through an AI pendant.

The approaches reflect different ideas about personal AI: visual devices capture the places and activities that shape a day, while audio-based ones preserve its conversations.

But a fuller record doesn’t necessarily make for a fuller life. As AI moves deeper into our daily lives, do we really need it to remember everything—or is forgetting part of being human?

item.title: Tencent releases Hy4 model weights with million-token context
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Tencent released the weights of its flagship Hy4 AI model on Friday, allowing developers to download and deploy the model themselves. The release follows Hy4’s initial launch on November 4 and makes the flagship available under the Apache 2.0 license, which permits commercial use and modification. Hy4 supports text, image and video understanding, with a […]
item.content:encoded:
Tencent released the weights of its flagship Hy4 AI model on Friday, allowing developers to download and deploy the model themselves. The release follows Hy4’s initial launch on November 4 and makes the flagship available under the Apache 2.0 license, which permits commercial use and modification.

Hy4 supports text, image and video understanding, with a context window of about one million tokens. Its mixture-of-experts language backbone contains 770 billion parameters, with 49 billion activated for each token. Tencent says the model improves on Hy4 preview in instruction following, long-context understanding, extended tasks and research.

The model supports workflows spanning graphical interfaces and command-line tools, alongside frontend development, game development and office tasks. Tencent provides deployment instructions for vLLM and SGLang, as well as fine-tuning resources and a safety evaluation card. The flagship’s release follows the separate opening of the smaller Hy4 flash model. [Tencent]

item.title: Ex-Qwen chief’s Pragmatik Labs raises funding at $5 billion valuation
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Pragmatik Labs, the AI startup founded by former Alibaba Qwen leader Lin Junyang, has raised new funding at a $5 billion valuation, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The round raised tens of millions of dollars, with new investors including HyT Capital, CDH Investments and automaker Geely. The valuation is 2.5 […]
item.content:encoded:
Pragmatik Labs, the AI startup founded by former Alibaba Qwen leader Lin Junyang, has raised new funding at a $5 billion valuation, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The round raised tens of millions of dollars, with new investors including HyT Capital, CDH Investments and automaker Geely.

The valuation is 2.5 times the $2 billion assigned to the company during its first financing in August, when it raised several hundred million dollars. That round was co-led by Gaorong Ventures and HSG, with participation from Tencent and a Shanghai government-backed investment fund.

Lin left Alibaba in March and established the Shanghai-based company over the summer. Pragmatik is developing next-generation AI agents for digital and physical environments. Its founder previously helped lead development of Alibaba’s Qwen model family, giving the young research company a prominent technical pedigree as it competes for funding and talent in China’s AI market. [Bloomberg]

item.title: Alibaba uses its own chips to train next-generation Qwen model
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Alibaba is using chips developed by its semiconductor subsidiary T-Head to train its next Qwen model, CEO Eddie Wu said during the company’s quarterly earnings call on Thursday. Alibaba’s Bailian model platform is also providing inference services using Chinese-made chips. The disclosure extends T-Head’s role across both major stages of AI computing: training models and […]
item.content:encoded:
Alibaba is using chips developed by its semiconductor subsidiary T-Head to train its next Qwen model, CEO Eddie Wu said during the company’s quarterly earnings call on Thursday. Alibaba’s Bailian model platform is also providing inference services using Chinese-made chips.

The disclosure extends T-Head’s role across both major stages of AI computing: training models and running them to answer user requests. Bailian, known internationally as Model Studio, provides access to models and tools for building AI applications.

Wu said coordination between Alibaba’s own chips and models would improve computing costs and application development efficiency. He also argued that the company’s full-stack AI infrastructure would give it an advantage within China’s domestic computing supply chain. The training work connects two core parts of Alibaba’s AI investment: its Qwen model family and the hardware supporting its cloud services. [CLS, in Chinese]

The six-seat model introduces BYD’s DMS hybrid platform, while the top trim features a steering wheel that folds away to free up cabin space. The Ti9 measures 5.27 meters long, with a 3.13-meter wheelbase and […]
item.content:encoded:
BYD’s Fang Cheng Bao brand launched the Ti9 plug-in hybrid SUV on Thursday, priced from RMB 279,900 to RMB 329,900. The six-seat model introduces BYD’s DMS hybrid platform, while the top trim features a steering wheel that folds away to free up cabin space.

The Ti9 measures 5.27 meters long, with a 3.13-meter wheelbase and three rows of two seats. Its folding-cockpit version combines the retractable steering wheel with a reclining driver’s seat and a panoramic display. The steering wheel takes about 10 seconds to fold. Across the range, equipment includes a 30-inch central screen, rear-wheel steering and BYD’s God’s Eye B driver-assistance system.

A 1.5-liter turbocharged engine works with front and rear electric motors producing a combined 400 kW. The 66.5 kWh second-generation Blade Battery provides a claimed 400 kilometers of electric range under China’s CLTC cycle, with combined range of 1,630 kilometers. BYD quotes a 0–100 km/h time of 4.8 seconds. [PCauto, in Chinese]

Powered by the Kirin 9030S chip, the wide-screen handset debuts an AI-focused edition of HarmonyOS 7 that lets users request services through natural-language conversations. The phone puts an animated […]
item.content:encoded:
Huawei launched its new smartphone brand OSTA and its first handset, the O1 Pro, on Friday, with introductory prices ranging from RMB 5,499 to RMB 8,799. Powered by the Kirin 9030S chip, the wide-screen handset debuts an AI-focused edition of HarmonyOS 7 that lets users request services through natural-language conversations.

The phone puts an animated assistant on a system-level AI screen, allowing users to issue instructions without first finding an app. Huawei says the system connects more than 2,100 system functions and over 500 ecosystem skills, supporting tasks across services including Alipay, Xiaohongshu, JD.com and Taobao. It also uses contextual information to recommend services and maintains memory through Huawei’s Xiaoyi Space.

Huawei executive Richard Yu positioned OSTA as a new consumer brand built around AI. The launch gives Huawei a separate platform for testing how assistants can become a central part of smartphone navigation and service delivery. [STAR Market Daily, in Chinese]

item.title: Tencent says Hunyuan Hy4 flash surpasses 50 trillion tokens in first-day usage
item.dc:creator: Jessie Wu
item.description: The rise of lightweight AI models is challenging the notion that bigger is always better. Tencent’s Hunyuan said on Wednesday that Hy4 flash processed more than 50 trillion tokens on its first day after launching on November 16, marking the highest first-day usage among models in the Hunyuan series. Hy4 flash’s strong debut was also […]
item.content:encoded:
The rise of lightweight AI models is challenging the notion that bigger is always better. Tencent’s Hunyuan said on Wednesday that Hy4 flash processed more than 50 trillion tokens on its first day after launching on November 16, marking the highest first-day usage among models in the Hunyuan series.

Hy4 flash’s strong debut was also reflected in its performance across different platforms. On OpenRouter’s daily LLM leaderboard, the model ranked first on November 17.

Tencent also said that on its WorkBuddy platform, Hy4 flash recorded 10 times the first-day usage of its predecessor, Hy4 preview, and had helped complete more than 50 million real-world user tasks.

According to Tencent, Hy4 flash uses a hybrid activation architecture and has 224 billion parameters in total, including 64 billion Engram parameters, while activating 12 billion parameters during inference.

The model also supports multimodal processing and a context window of up to 1 million tokens. Tencent said its generation speed reaches around 200 tokens per second. But what makes Hy4 flash particularly noteworthy is how it balances performance and cost.

According to Tencent’s pricing, the model charges just 0.5 yuan ($0.07) per million input tokens and 2 yuan ($0.3) per million output tokens, with cached input tokens costing as little as 0.02 yuan ($0.003) per million.

Based on Tencent’s internal WorkIndex benchmark, which evaluates common office tasks, Hy4 flash costs just one-thirteenth as much as Hy4 preview and one-twentieth as much as Hy4 to complete a single task. Its cost is also around one-eighth that of mainstream lightweight models in the same category.

These advantages make it particularly suitable for high-frequency office tasks, including creating and editing presentations, document processing, spreadsheet repair, audio and video processing, and visual understanding.

The launch also comes after an earlier surge in demand for Hy4. When the model debuted on WorkBuddy on November 4, demand driven by its agent capabilities exceeded expectations, with many users hitting their usage limits on the first day. Tencent subsequently expanded its Hy4 inference clusters tenfold and increased free usage quotas.

This time, however, the team appears to have made more extensive preparations for high concurrency ahead of Hy4 flash’s launch, with no widespread usage-limit issues reported so far.

The development also reflects a broader shift in the AI industry’s competitive landscape.

As daily token usage in China continues to grow, tokens are increasingly becoming an important metric for measuring AI adoption. Meanwhile, local governments across the country are introducing new measures, ranging from computing power and model vouchers to token-based financing, to make AI services more affordable.

Competition is no longer just about parameter counts or model performance. Delivering strong results while keeping operating costs low is becoming equally important.

Hy4 flash’s 50-trillion-token debut sends a clear signal: the market needs not only more capable AI models, but also models that are affordable enough for frequent, everyday use.

However, there is still a gap between strong first-day usage and long-term commercial value. Competition among lightweight AI models may increasingly come down to more than just pricing and token usage.

The real challenge is delivering solutions to real-world business needs consistently and reliably, while keeping overall costs low. For Tencent’s Hunyuan, Hy4 flash’s strong debut is a promising start, but its ability to turn initial usage momentum into sustained user value will be a key test going forward.

Prices start at AED 169,900 for the SU7, AED 184,900 for the YU7 and AED 209,900 for the SkyNomad. The dealer lists December 2026 availability for initial versions. The sales channel also offers leasing and […]
item.content:encoded:
UAE dealer Gargash Prime Automotive has opened preorders for Xiaomi’s SU7 electric sedan, YU7 electric SUV and SkyNomad range-extended SUV. Prices start at AED 169,900 for the SU7, AED 184,900 for the YU7 and AED 209,900 for the SkyNomad. The dealer lists December 2026 availability for initial versions.

The sales channel also offers leasing and local after-sales packages, including warranties of up to five years or 150,000 kilometers and maintenance coverage of up to 60,000 kilometers. Additional variants are listed for February 2027 delivery. The listings give UAE buyers a local purchase and service channel as Xiaomi prepares its broader overseas automotive expansion. [ChinaEVHome]

The architecture combines a mobile security processor with an embedded secure-element chip and has received CCRC EAL5+ security certification, according to Huawei. The two security components work […]
item.content:encoded:
Huawei disclosed details of the Kirin 9050 series’ security architecture on Wednesday, saying the mobile chips support post-quantum cryptography and have undergone testing for resistance to quantum attacks. The architecture combines a mobile security processor with an embedded secure-element chip and has received CCRC EAL5+ security certification, according to Huawei.

The two security components work together to support secure boot, data protection, privacy and communications security. Post-quantum cryptography is designed to protect information against future quantum computers that could compromise widely used encryption methods. The disclosure follows Huawei’s recent technical breakdowns of the Kirin 9050’s computing, imaging and display capabilities. [IT Home, in Chinese]

item.title: Musk pledges to boost Tesla production in China
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the company would continue increasing production in China during a meeting with China Council for the Promotion of International Trade Chairman Ren Hongbin in Shenzhen on Thursday. Musk, who was visiting the city for APEC-related events, also described himself as a “super fan” of China. Tesla’s Shanghai factory is central […]
item.content:encoded:
Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the company would continue increasing production in China during a meeting with China Council for the Promotion of International Trade Chairman Ren Hongbin in Shenzhen on Thursday. Musk, who was visiting the city for APEC-related events, also described himself as a “super fan” of China.

Tesla’s Shanghai factory is central to its global manufacturing and export network. It produces the Model 3 and Model Y for buyers in China and overseas, making any further increase in output relevant to both markets. Musk’s remarks signal continued commitment to Chinese production, although he provided no timetable or volume target. [IT Home, in Chinese]
